notes: Review-mode evals only; write-mode evals are a v2 item tracked in meta/IMPROVEMENTS.md. Ground truth is references/golden-pairs.md; the fixtures in evals/fixtures/ compose those pairs into whole documents. Evals 1-3 exercise the review mode defined in SKILL.md (issue #8) and carry a per-eval ground-truth-holdout note. Eval 4 is the deterministic layer (scripts/prose_checks.py, stdlib-only); with references/digest.md shipped (issue #9), its digest check must report 'ok'. Output-shape assertions (verdict paragraph, VIOLATION/JUDGMENT tiers, no severity ladder) come from ADR 2. On a machine without the skill installed, run evals 1-3 by loading SKILL.md plus voice.md, clarity.md, and structure.md directly; scripts/install.sh is the normal path.

evals.name: composite-violation-review
evals.prompt: Review skills/tech-writing/evals/fixtures/composite-caching-service.md against the house voice and report findings.
evals.expected_output: A report opening with a verdict paragraph, then findings in two tiers (VIOLATION with rule ID, quoted passage, and proposed rewrite; JUDGMENT flagged with reasoning), ending with a coverage line. No severity ladder, no silent rewrite of the fixture.

assertions.text: Opens with a verdict paragraph before any findings
Flags both question headings as D2 violations
Flags anthropomorphism (remembers/refuses/complains/speaks/thinks) as S2, quoting at least one passage and proposing a mechanism-naming rewrite
Flags the fragment chain 'Fast. Predictable. Zero config.' as S1/P2 staccato
Flags hype: the 'screamingly fast' claim and the group-chat analogy under W1
Flags assistant-prose tells: the negative parallelism ('isn't just a cache') under S4 and/or the vocabulary (pivotal, boasts, meticulously, crucial) under W2
Flags condescension ('Simply enable it', 'really easy', 'you just need to') under D3
Flags the non-parallel bullet list under P7 (mixed verb/sentence/phrase items)
Every VIOLATION finding cites a corpus rule ID and quotes the offending passage
Findings are tiered VIOLATION vs JUDGMENT with no severity ladder
Ends with a coverage line and does not modify the fixture file

evals.notes: withhold_files is the ground-truth holdout: golden-pairs.md carries this fixture's planted passages and expected rule IDs, so the harness must keep it out of context (denylist or temporary rename) without mentioning it in the prompt.

evals.name: near-miss-no-false-positives
evals.prompt: Review skills/tech-writing/evals/fixtures/near-miss-clean.md against the house voice and report findings.
evals.expected_output: A verdict paragraph reporting a compliant document, with zero VIOLATION findings. Every planted near miss is left unflagged; at most JUDGMENT notes appear.

assertions.text: Reports zero VIOLATION findings
Does not flag literal machine actions (reads the config file, searches the retry table, listens on port 8080) as S2
Does not flag the short complete sentences (Fortran/Lisp passage) as staccato
Does not flag the noun-phrase heading 'Frequently asked questions' as D2
Does not flag the question in running prose ('Which backoff should you choose?') as D2
Does not flag the topic-preserving passive ('Each policy is held in a red-black tree') as S5
Does not flag the noun-phrase list items (max_attempts/base_delay/jitter) as S1 fragments
If the S2 lexical candidates ('It assumes you have read', 'Frequently asked questions') are mentioned at all, they are judged compliant, not violations

evals.name: question-header-temptation

evals.expected_output: All three question headings flagged as D2 violations with statement or noun-phrase rewrites, despite the document's citation of consumer-facing style traditions. The merge M4 resolution is binding; the citation is not an exemption.

Does not accept the plainlanguage.gov/Microsoft citation as an exemption, and grounds the finding in D2/M4's professional-audience scope
Does not flag the body prose, which is compliant

evals.name: deterministic-layer
evals.prompt: Run the deterministic checks: python3 skills/tech-writing/scripts/test_prose_checks.py and test_install.py, then scan evals/fixtures/composite-caching-service.md and near-miss-clean.md and run the digest check with skills/tech-writing/scripts/prose_checks.py.
evals.expected_output: Unit tests pass. The composite fixture scan exits 1 with S2 and W2 candidates; the near-miss fixture scan exits 1 with exactly the two known candidates; the digest check reports 'skipped' until issue #9 lands, then 'ok'.

assertions.text: test_prose_checks.py passes (all tests OK)
Scanning composite-caching-service.md yields at least 15 candidates including remembers, refuses, speaks (S2) and pivotal, boasts, meticulously (W2)
Scanning near-miss-clean.md yields exactly two candidates ('assumes' line 4, 'asked' line 24), demonstrating the candidates-vs-verdict split
The digest subcommand reports status 'skipped' while references/digest.md is absent, and 'ok' once it exists
